caption_text:
2025年開年，我們榮幸繼續攜手為永豐銀行DAWAY信用卡打造全新升級形象！

新版形象以「掩不住鋒芒」為概念，融合銀色光芒與簡約設計語言，呈現每一次提卡消費鋒芒畢露的瞬間，詮釋持卡人內斂卻耀眼的個人風格。

「消費生活的内涵，不只清晰透明，更是漂亮有形」

當信用卡不再只是支付工具，從取卡、付款到收妥卡片的每個瞬間，都是一場名為「風格金融」細膩的生活儀式。透過設計、從信用卡通路優惠溝通到社群內容應用，我們以「清晰透明」為視覺應用主題，創造連貫形象，讓信用卡品牌個性穿透所有溝通的媒介、走入消費者生活，創造共鳴。

caption_text:
A short making-of of a logo promo project I created for the one and only @vmgroupe in New York.
For visual reference and inspiration, we visited one of the most incredible places in the world — Lion’s Rock in Sigiriya, Sri Lanka. The trip turned into a bit more of an adventure than expected, as heavy storms and hurricanes had destroyed roads and disrupted communication across parts of the country while we were there. Despite all the challenges, we still managed to make it there.
Moments like this remind me how grateful I am to do what I do. Exploring places, studying textures, light and atmosphere, translating those impressions into motion design is one of the most rewarding parts of my work.

Pretty awesome moment as I'm a big fan of these guys and their content - this is Wren and Sam from @corridordigital sitting with Tim Miller as they react to the @lovedeathandrobots episode I helped do the lighting for in @unrealengine. 

Not only was it cool to see some of my work featured on their staple show "VFX Artists React " but both Sam and Wren are blown away that this was all done in Unreal. 

Once again, congrats to the whole team for putting together one of the more impressive Unreal Engine projects out there.

caption_text:
New @unrealengine lighting work! This was another fun collaboration with @lunchbqx who did a phenomenal job directing again. 

We have a few different looks here and I'll break them down a bit starting out with the garage environments.

We were looking to achieve a dark, hazy cinematic look to match the mysterious nature of the shots - the garage door unveil if you will. I spent some time trying different sun directions, including very backlit from the far back windows but it wasn't feeling totally right. So eventually I found something that matched the intended moodyness but still looked interesting - we added some windows on the right side to create a back splash on the background just to separate the car edges a bit, and then added a cheated second sun to go through the trees and create a dappled effect on the pavement and garage door. There is more to it but that was the final lighting design in a nutshell. 

For the suburbs shots that come up next, the intention was to create an early morning sunrise look as opposed to a sunset look. And while they are similar I feel like there is more blueness in the ambience for an early morning look which is what I did for these. 

For the downtown environments, I really wanted to do something different than a low sun backlight, so we went a bit more with a high noon look that I think is really successful in selling these shots as photoreal. Going in and out of building shadows really helps the effect here too. 

Of course none of this would look right if the environment around the car and the cars themselves didnt look incredible, which they do here. So congrats to the team for all their hard work, it really paid off.

creator: thanu_lee
collection: 名單帳號 · 已分析參考
description: Beats iPhone 17 手機保護殼導演剪輯：岩石、纖維近景與微小球粒表面，殼體波紋變形、撞擊碎石和粒子層分離，多色產品及繩帶展示。

Working closely with the Beats team last year, we crafted a series of films for the launch of cases for iPhone 17.
Here’s the director’s cut, bringing together some of our favorite moments from all three commercials.

Production: @stevechoo_nyc @myactivedriveway 
Direction: Thanos Kagkalos, @stevechoo_nyc 
Design / Animation: Thanos Kagkalos, @itsriple @alesbalantic @tactyc.studio

caption_text:
A next step for my worlds - I wanted to build something that could run in almost any browser on almost any phone or laptop. The super nostalgic puzzle games I grew up on like Myst, Zork and Riven seemed like a good starting point as they can be pre rendered with all the AAA effects and coded simply in html and css. All built in 3D and then coded with some help from Claude. I’ve figured out the basic navigation - next step is to add some more rooms, puzzles and integrate an AI api as the house security system! 

#cinema4d #redshift3d #brutalistarchitecture #adventuregames #myst

caption_text:
A collaboration with @wintdesignlab , a design lab focused on sustainable product innovation, to investigate the potential benefits of using inflation in new packaging methods. This project aims to explore how harnessing air can lead to more durable and efficient ways of creating spaces and protecting goods at various scales.

Inspired by nature’s microstructures, this project journeys from the microscopic to the monumental. Structured into three chapters, the narrative explores a design methodology grounded in research, experimentation, and applied imagination.

My contribution sat on the R&D side and on the inflating tests. Only a handful of days of work, but I am glad I got to be part of this one. It pulls design, 3D, graphic design and motion design into the same film, and that mix of technique makes it rich and interesting.

Done at @protoeditions.xyz 

Team
CD: @jamesrearls 
AD: @notenough.fun 
3D+Gfx: @romain.rosi @karmazin198 @ali.rigby @jessica_ciupa 
Sound: @guignollll

caption_text:
Trying my hands at the reel trends too. 👋

“Tell me about yourself”  so here’s my version.

A little mix of what I’ve been exploring lately: 3D renders from my tech motion studies, CGI drink experiments, 3D type, and other motion design explorations.

Most of these are built in Cinema 4D + Redshift, just experimenting with different forms, materials, lighting, and movement.

creator: mariannesanche
collection: 最新貼文 · 待分析
description: 待分析：CG 判定、物件、動態、材質與顏色尚未完成核對。 本項暫為輪播封面，完整媒體拆分待後續分析。
caption_text:
I built a workflow that transforms images of people + their environment into a fully playable 3d game 🎮🖤 i Swipe to see how >>

The design + 3D of both the character and environment is done in @fuserstudio and the playable character template + level building is done in @unrealengine

Here’s a little preview of the Character Generator Workflow. From image to 2D character to 3D character. 

Same logic for the 3D scene. Start with an image, the workflow recreates it as a 2D retro game scene. Then, it extracts all the assets needed (first in 2D then in 3D).

I wanted a GTA vibe so I generated a lot of assets to build a city street

I imported all the scene assets in Unreal Engine to create a little street

With less than 20 assets I was able to create a pretty cool looking street in Unreal Engine

I used Unreal’s Third Person Template to turn my character into a playable third person pov character.

The final result is a playable level in Unreal Engine 🎮🖤 Let me know in the comments if you want a full length video on the whole process!!

INTRODUCING OUR NEXT JUDGE & FEATURED ARTIST. 

For the SODA Digital Art Exhibition 2027, we’re welcoming Daria Anise (@look.deva) to the jury and featuring her work as part of the exhibition in Sorrento.

3D artist working across procedural graphics, simulations, particles and hair, Daria creates worlds where vibrant colors, soft textures and surreal, slightly unhinged metaphors come together.

With around a decade of experience across motion design, VFX and immersive media, her practice sits at the intersection of art and technology. Her academic background in art and design, with a focus on information technologies, shapes an approach that combines creative experimentation with strong technical expertise.

We’re excited to bring her unique visual language to Sorrento and have her perspective as part of the SODA jury.

caption_text:
Untitled Spaces - Blender Short Film

This project is the result of my passion for architecture, interior design, cinematography and music. Everything you see is 100% CGI (no AI of course), created using the free 3D software @blender.official The score is also composed by me, and best enjoyed through some proper speakers or headphones. Hope you like it :)

I went deep into the compositing stage for this project, drawing lots of inspiration from mid century architectural magazines. When scanned in they usually show a combination of film characteristics, half toning and CMYK print misalignment from the printing stage as well as imperfections and artificial sharpening from the digital processing and scanning of the catalogues. I wondered what would happen if I tried transferring these looks onto video, which is what I've tried doing in this project. I think the imperfections and abnormalities in stuff is what gives it character and what makes it relatable and realistic. It's a shame that the Youtube compression is so tough though, so I'd recommend watching it in full 4K. 

The programs I used in the project was Blender for all of the set layout, modeling, lighting texturing and rendering. The compositing was done in After Effects and the final sequence was edited in Davinci Resolve. For the scoring, it was composed in Logic Pro X. 

All of these shots are inspired by real world architects and furniture designers such as: 

Rem Koolhaas, Charles & Ray Eames, John Lautner, Hans & Florence Knoll, Kazuo Shinohara, Bahk Jong Sun, Wilhelm Wagenfeld, Paul Rudolph, André Lurcat, Verner Panton and David Bowen.

If you want to get more insights into how this was made and get access to other assets, tutorials and add-ons you can support me through my Patreon, thank you:) #architectureart #architecturalfilm #architecturalvisuals #artandarchitecture #architecturalphotography #conceptualarchitecture #experimentalarchitecture #architecturecinema #architectureaesthetics #architecturemotion #architectureinmotion #archfilm #archivizual #designfilm #architecturalstorytelling #visualarchitecture #modernistarchitecture #brutalistarchitecture #minimalarchitecture #blenderrender

caption_text:
Sound by @echoic_audio 

Botànica Binària - An ode to inner healing cycles within our bodies and surroundings. A series of floral explorations to represent the idea of kinetic bouquets around human environments.

Exploring how organic beauty can transform into geometric patterns and data sequences creating visual landscapes where natural and digital elements merge. The combination of computer generated visual effects and a soundtrack blending organic and synthetic sounds invites us to think about the relationship between the biological and the virtual, offering an alternative to today’s landscape.

Exhibited at Melbourne @rollienation shop / gallery / showroom during May and October 2024 - Girona Temps de Flors 2025 @tempsdeflors - Brava Arts Weekend @brava_arts 

Huge thanks to my all time sound buddies @echoic_audio for such an amazing soundtrack..

caption_text:
I built this luminance-driven sprite triggering system in After Effects (it’s a mouthful) to use an input composition such as noise, shape layers, or footage, to drive time remapping across a grid of sprite precomps.
Anything inside the sprite can be triggered, with additional controls for grid resolution, gamma, threshold, and retriggering. ⚪️🔵🟢🟠🤓

caption_text:
Temporal Strata | audiovisual dome experience
World premiere in Miami

Temporal Strata takes the materiality of time as its point of departure, treating time as strata capable of sedimentation, disturbance, and continuous formation. Within the immersive field of the dome, sound and image are woven into a single perceptual space, displacing linear narrative as the mode through which time is apprehended. Time is instead progressively recalibrated in the act of looking and listening, as rhythms elongate and restructure and attention shifts between micro-variations. The work invites consciousness to contract into a single point, converting time from abstract measure into a state perceived through sound and image. Amid the accumulation of texture and the collapse of space, one begins to gauge the sense of presence that each breath inscribes.

title: Cymbal Interaction · Animation Test
creator: jaevnstroem
collection: 最新貼文 · 待分析
description: 待分析：CG 判定、物件、動態、材質與顏色尚未完成核對。
caption_text:
Cymbal interaction test - animation & audio //

This is an early test of modeling, animating and rendering believable cymbal behavior, for a bigger project of a complete drum kit animated and rendered in Cinema 4D

The drumstick is traditionally (and somewhat sloppy) animated using keyframes, the cymbal utilizes Signal by @greyscalegorilla for the tilting and the micro vibrations. There are two Signal tags, constantly running in a loop, one on the rotation axis of a null, and another on the strength parameter of a bend deformer (actually it's two bend deformers, but one is just following the other, but flipped) and I'm just manually keyframing the volume of the Signal tags to correspond with the hits.

The audio is made using Superior Drummer 3 by @toontrack which I'll also be using when I finally get to animate the full kit!

🎨 Artist of the Week

What happens when you stop asking, “How is this supposed to work?” and start asking, “What if I tried it anyway?”

That’s the creative philosophy behind @jaevnstroem’s work.

As a motion designer based in Denmark, Daniel approaches every personal project as an open-ended R&D session. He intentionally combines techniques that shouldn’t work together, imposes creative limitations, and experiments until something unexpected happens.

It’s no surprise that Signal has become a staple in his workflow, helping bring those experiments to life through seamless motion.

Swipe through for a collection of animations that prove curiosity is one of the most powerful creative tools.

caption_text:
DeepBook is the liquidity layer built to strengthen Sui’s DeFi ecosystem. At its core are three primitives: Spot, Margin and Predict, brought together into one composable stack that gives developers the foundation to build financial products that don’t exist yet.

That ambition shaped the brand from the start. Our north star was to take something deeply technical and make it accessible to a much broader audience of builders and traders without stripping away the complexity that makes DeepBook powerful.

We built a visual language around that idea, combining illustration, motion and a modular pattern system with an interactive digital experience designed to make the technology easier to understand, explore and engage with.

The result is a brand and website that gives DeepBook a clearer identity as infrastructure for what comes next on Sui.
Our work covered brand direction, visual identity, illustration, motion, website design and development, and social.

The Paul Kalkbrenner site @iampaulkalkbrenner just picked up Site of the Day and the Developer Award on Awwwards.

Two recognitions in one, which says something about both sides of the project: a visual direction built on a clean, minimal foundation with a retro-inspired palette, and a build careful enough to hold all the motion and interaction without ever getting in the way.

We’ve been working with Paul across a range of projects for a few years now, so this one feels good for the whole collaboration, not just the site.
If you’re into his music, the site is worth a visit on its own: his story, the full discography, current tour dates, and the shop are all there.

Our work covered website design, motion, interactions, and development.

title: Swatch · Colors of Joy Process
creator: guido.glid
collection: 最新貼文 · 待分析
description: 待分析：CG 判定、物件、動態、材質與顏色尚未完成核對。
caption_text:
Our @swatch Colors of Joy film just received Video of the Year at @motiondesignawards ♥️
 
We are really happy about this one, mostly because when we made this video, we decided not to show the project in the usual way. Even though Colors of Joy was part of a full 360 campaign, we wanted to show it through the eyes of the creatives behind it. So this film became a sort of collage of process.... raw ideas, unfinished renders, previews, tests, playful moments, things half-built, things still searching for their final form.

Probably 80% of what you see in that video is not “finished” in the traditional sense. And that was exactly the point. We wanted to show the energy behind the work. The exploration. The experimentation. The fun. The human thinking behind the final campaign.

This award shows that the community still cares deeply about the PROCESS and HOW things are made. Not just what the final image looks like, but what is behind it..... the attempts, the doubts, the play, the decisions, the people who made it, what was tried, what failed, what evolved.

At a moment when final images are becoming easier and easier to generate, this feels like an important reminder to everyone: the value is not only in the final pixel. It is in the vision, the craft, the taste, the time, the story, the experimentation, and the human energy behind it.

That is what gives a project its soul.

It means a lot to see that raw ideas, unfinished moments, and honest creative process can still resonate.

And maybe that is exactly why our videos cut through the noise.

A huge thank you to everyone involved in this project, to Motion Design Awards for the recognition, and to the creative community for embracing unconventional work like this.

@vincentschwenk, @_fran_rossi, @sergiofuego_estudio, @darling.motion, @hyper.chris, @anna.hariaha, @tsymbal3d, @hoffwerr, @leazarev, @_noi_berlin, @joanmoreno.tv, @ilmarcolino @guido.glid ♥️ 

More at www.glidstudio.ch

#MotionDesign #MotionGraphics #CreativeProcess #BehindTheScenes #GlidStudio

Material [Fundamentals]

Full circle: Photographing a 3D render.

In the next phase of our crossover experiment with @mariuswhansen, we flipped the traditional workflow on its head.

After finishing our 3D compositing, we returned to Marius’s studio with our final renders displayed on high-resolution screens. By re-photographing those displays using physical lenses, anamorphic correction, and multi-exposure techniques, we captured beautifully unexpected in-camera results.

The resulting images have the ethereal presence of genuine physical objects, grounded by practical studio lighting, and blur the line between tangible reality and digital artefact.​

Link to the full case study in our bio. 🔗

Material [Fundamentals]​

From the photography studio to our digital arena.

The first phase of our [Fundamentals] project with @mariuswhansen began in his photography studio, surrounded by equipment and select Tiffany jewellery pieces. 

Being in the room together was vital, as we watched Marius capture intricate details, directional light, and the raw materiality of the physical pieces. 

These reference images served as a precise baseline. As we prepared digital CAD models of the jewellery, we translated real-world insights, applied nuanced material behaviours and observed subtle surface imperfections taken directly from the shoot.

🔗 Link to the full case study in bio

caption_text:
I’m sharing a free @cavalry.app script that adds new features to the built-in Convex Hull tool.
You can add obstacle shapes and control the overall form to create different variations.
The source code is available, so you can download it, edit it, and customize it for your own needs.
My previous Soft Cell script is also now open source.
I’ve been extremely busy recently and probably won’t have much time to maintain or fix bugs, so I decided to share everything openly instead.
I hope these two scripts can help with your learning and creative process!
Link in bio.

caption_text:
Been messing around with some cell-style animation lately and somehow ended up making a whole @cavalry.app script 😅
It’s mainly built with JS Shapes, and tbh, Codex did most of the coding. I was basically the ideas guy—testing stuff, breaking stuff, and asking for endless changes until it finally worked lol.
Definitely not calling myself a “developer” here. I just wanted a nice little system that makes it easier for me to animate this kind of thing. The result is giving slightly cursed Voronoi shader vibes 👀
If anyone wants to try it, feel free to DM me and I’ll send you the free version.

caption_text:
🇬🇧 🖥️ The art of Federico Piccirillo: 3D artist & motion designer

There are artists who use 3D to recreate reality. Federico Piccirillo uses it to reinvent it. In this post, we take a brief look at the Italian motion designer and art director whose work creates images suspended somewhere between the possible and the imaginary, oscillating between surrealism and hyperrealism. Each animation becomes the construction of a digital space where light and materials, in just a few seconds, are able to tell a story. Simple forms, minimalist environments, and warm color palettes become tools for creating images that feel both familiar and impossible, often elevated by a perfectly chosen soundtrack. The reason I decided to feature Federico on this page is his close albeit indirect connection to the world of cinema, recalling a cinematic language that does not merely imitate reality, but transforms it into emotion. This approach is evident throughout his work, where every frame feels as though it were conceived as a shot from a film.

After earning a degree in Graphic Design and Visual Communication in Florence, Piccirillo began his professional career as a motion designer at Nerdo Studio. He later chose to work as a freelance artist, specializing in 3D and collaborating on campaigns for brands such as Google, Nike, Apple, LEGO, IBM, Oppo, and many others. What makes his work truly distinctive, however, is not a single recognizable style. On the contrary, Piccirillo deliberately avoids confining himself to one visual language, constantly experimenting with new aesthetics and new ways of telling stories through movement. This ongoing exploration demonstrates that 3D is not merely a technical tool, but a powerful expressive medium capable of transforming ideas, emotions, and imagination into living images.

caption_text:
This fluid study was built around a custom 2D Pyro workflow.

The idea originally came from an R&D task I was working on for a client project earlier this year. I liked the underlying behavior enough to revisit it later and push the technique further as a personal experiment.

I first created an initial simulation focused on the main velocity field, while also generating UVs internally as an additional 2D Pyro field. That first sim then became the advection driver for the bubbles and their velocity, allowing them to inherit the motion and flow of the fluid in a more natural way.

After that, I created a second fluid simulation using only the velocity from the first Pyro setup, combined with collisions and bubble velocity. This made the fluid react to spheres moving across its surface, changing the internal mixing and creating more dynamic interaction.

I also experimented with a non-divergent workflow in COPs, but for this particular look it was missing some of the organic, naturally unstable motion that I still get from the old 2D Pyro Solver.

A fun experiment in using Pyro not only as smoke, but as a flexible field-based solver for art-directable fluid motion and procedural detail.

A project for SK-II LXP that I was fortunate to be part of in 2024 during my time at @arsthanea 

Looking back, this was one of those projects that taught me a tremendous amount of knowledge. From R&D and look development to the final visuals, it was a challenging and rewarding experience that helped shape many of the skills I use today.

Massive thanks to the entire team for making it happen.

All created in Houdini and rendered with Redshift.

A closer look at the trophy designs behind our Video of the Year celebration. 🏆

This idea turned into dozens of sketches, tests, and variations before we landed on the final design.
The whole celebration piece was created to mark an incredible milestone for our studio, combining moments from the award-winning films, custom design elements, and a whole lot of love for motion.

We're still incredibly grateful for the recognition and proud of everyone who helped bring these projects to life.

Stay tuned for what's next. ✨

@saloondesign is our new experimental design lab, a space where we get to play, explore, and bring unique, functional objects to life. Just like with Stylo, our goal is to push creativity in thoughtful, sustainable ways that make everyday spaces feel more beautiful and intentional.

We’re starting with lighting. Using 3D printing lets us design without the usual limits of manufacturing, creating lamps that feel personal, sculptural, and timeless.

caption_text:
“The Ascension of PAK” and “The Exodus of PAK” are two sides of the same visual and sonic idea.

For the sound design, I wanted the relationship between the two pieces to feel almost like looking at the same image through a negative: familiar shapes, movements, and gestures, but emotionally inverted.
Rather than creating two completely separate soundtracks, I approached them as sonic mirror images. The same core sonic language exists in both pieces, but its emotional weight, frequency, texture, dynamics, and spatial character are transformed between the positive and negative versions.

"Ascension" lives in the world of emergence, elevation, expansion, and light. Its sounds are designed to feel as though they are pulling upward and opening outward. Longer tonal elements, rising textures, resonances, and brighter high-frequency detail help reinforce the sense of movement and transformation.

"Exodus" takes that same conceptual DNA and turns it inside out. Sounds become darker, heavier, more restrained, and more gravitational. Where Ascension suggests expansion, Exodus suggests contraction. Where one rises, the other falls.

A major part of the process was building the sound effects around the physical movement of the visuals. Every transition, distortion, flicker, rotation, flash, and change in form became an opportunity for a sonic event. Impacts were synchronized to visual hits, granular textures followed digital artifacts, tonal sweeps reinforced movement through space, and subtle environmental layers helped give the abstract imagery a sense of physical presence.

I wanted the sound design to respond to the black-and-white inversion itself. The visual negative isn't simply a different grade—it changes how the image feels. I treated the audio in the same way.

The two tracks share DNA, but their emotional frequencies are reversed.

The goal was for the two pieces to feel like they could exist independently, while revealing something completely different when experienced together—as two reflections of the same sonic and visual object.

caption_text:
Lately I’ve been thinking a lot about the connection I share with my family and the people I love. This feeling of homesickness turned into a project about closeness, memory and warmth.
I wanted this animation to feel alive. Not sad, but full of color and energy.
Every scene means something to me, and I hope it resonates with anyone who misses home from time to time. 🧵✨

Directed & Animated 🎬 by Daria Togunova @daytogu 
Beautiful Sound Design 🎶 by Aaron Graham @aarongrahammusic

Azimuth has been officially nominated for the VES Awards 2026 in the category: Outstanding Visual Effects in a Student Project🏆

Since 2023, the long-standing collaboration between @satisfaction_agency and @christoph_strohfeld has brought a series of projects for Samsonite to life.
Christoph Strohfeld led the 3D production, working closely with @tactyc.studio as a trusted CGI partner. Their technical expertise, professionalism and dedication have been an invaluable part of the process, helping us deliver the work smoothly and at the highest level.
We finally took the time to bring together some of the work from the past years and want to thank everyone who contributed along the way. A lot of talented people have been part of these productions, and we truly appreciate the trust, commitment and collaboration behind each one.
Looking back with gratitude — and forward to what’s next.  #design #cgi #3D #samsonite #travel

caption_text:
To Her We Return, (2026) - collaboration with artist @zaynqahtani for her solo show The Whisperings at @kristinhjellegjerdegallery 

We created an ancient doorway with living moss and dilmun symbols to frame the huge portal. The animation reflects Zayn’s primary sculpting material - abalone shell, with ripples capturing the same index of refraction as the real material to create a living, ever-changing representation of it in her exhibition.

Exhibition is on until 12 May 🕳️🏃✨ go and catch the portal before it disappears into another realm…

caption_text:
After a hiatus of a few years, it is time for me to return to design.

In recent years, I deliberately set this aspect of my work aside to focus more on photography. It was a period that allowed me to grow, refine my eye, and—above all—see things differently.

Now, I want to bring these two experiences together.

Returning to design with a fresh perspective, enriched by photography, imagery, composition, light, and everything I have learned over the past few years.

There is no question of simply picking up where I left off.

The idea is to head in a new direction.
Something more contemporary. More creative. More aligned with what inspires me today.

Photography + Design. A new chapter.

caption_text:
Lately, I’ve been building a foundational system designed to support everything I want to ship through rapid prototyping and AI-assisted development. While "vibe coding" lets us spin up ideas in minutes, it also exposes a major gap: without strong structural boundaries, rapid code quickly turns into a black box of technical debt.

The goal isn't just to build fast; it's to define efficient, transparent patterns that keep the architecture predictable.

Some progress on the token framework. It currently supports:
→ Multi-axis theming contracts for dynamic UI skins.
→ System modes configured for macOS and Windows structural paradigms.
→ A wallpaper package that extracts and feeds dynamic primary colors back into the UI.
→ Granular exposed controls for fluid typography, corner radiuses, and system iconography.
→ A unified theme package that instantly drops into independent micro-sites consuming the same tokens.

It’s easier than ever to code something visually stunning. But because UI is deeply subjective and constantly evolving, the real engineering challenge changes:

How do you build an infrastructure that isn't just adaptive to any art direction—but remains maintainable, deterministic, and meaningful?

Still exploring the edges of this, but unwrapping that black box is the part worth solving.

Live site: https://os.atom63.io/
Deeply inspired by @ryo.lu

#Victionary 新書 #ThreeDimensional 編輯特選作品！
我們榮幸入選 Victionary @victionworkshop 全新出版的《ThreeDimensional》，作為具國際能見度的設計出版品牌，Victionary 長期以精準選題與跨國視覺案例策展聞名。
.
此次出版的《ThreeDimensional》聚焦 3D 技術在品牌識別、視覺語言與敘事結構中的應用，呈現三維設計在當代品牌表現中逐漸成為核心語彙的趨勢。
.
本次收錄「Taipei Design Award 2023」及 「The 34th Golden Melody Awards & Festival」反映兩件作品在視覺敘事與立體化語言上的表現，並呈現當代品牌影像創作在創意與技術之間的連動與可能性。

caption_text:
To Her We Return, (2026) - collaboration with artist @zaynqahtani for her solo show The Whisperings at @kristinhjellegjerdegallery 

We created an ancient doorway with living moss and dilmun symbols to frame the huge portal. The animation reflects Zayn’s primary sculpting material - abalone shell, with ripples capturing the same index of refraction as the real material to create a living, ever-changing representation of it in her exhibition.

Exhibition is on until 12 May 🕳️🏃✨ go and catch the portal before it disappears into another realm…

caption_text:
To Her We Return, (2026) - collaboration with artist @zaynqahtani for her solo show The Whisperings at @kristinhjellegjerdegallery 

We created an ancient doorway with living moss and dilmun symbols to frame the huge portal. The animation reflects Zayn’s primary sculpting material - abalone shell, with ripples capturing the same index of refraction as the real material to create a living, ever-changing representation of it in her exhibition.

Exhibition is on until 12 May 🕳️🏃✨ go and catch the portal before it disappears into another realm…

Since 2023, the long-standing collaboration between @satisfaction_agency and @christoph_strohfeld has brought a series of projects for Samsonite to life.
Christoph Strohfeld led the 3D production, working closely with @tactyc.studio as a trusted CGI partner. Their technical expertise, professionalism and dedication have been an invaluable part of the process, helping us deliver the work smoothly and at the highest level.
We finally took the time to bring together some of the work from the past years and want to thank everyone who contributed along the way. A lot of talented people have been part of these productions, and we truly appreciate the trust, commitment and collaboration behind each one.
Looking back with gratitude — and forward to what’s next.  #design #cgi #3D #samsonite #travel

caption_text:
Since 2023, the long-standing collaboration between @satisfaction_agency and @christoph_strohfeld has brought a series of projects for Samsonite to life.
Christoph Strohfeld led the 3D production, working closely with @tactyc.studio as a trusted CGI partner. Their technical expertise, professionalism and dedication have been an invaluable part of the process, helping us deliver the work smoothly and at the highest level.
We finally took the time to bring together some of the work from the past years and want to thank everyone who contributed along the way. A lot of talented people have been part of these productions, and we truly appreciate the trust, commitment and collaboration behind each one.
Looking back with gratitude — and forward to what’s next.  #design #cgi #3D #samsonite #travel

caption_text:
“The Ascension of PAK” and “The Exodus of PAK” are two sides of the same visual and sonic idea.

For the sound design, I wanted the relationship between the two pieces to feel almost like looking at the same image through a negative: familiar shapes, movements, and gestures, but emotionally inverted.
Rather than creating two completely separate soundtracks, I approached them as sonic mirror images. The same core sonic language exists in both pieces, but its emotional weight, frequency, texture, dynamics, and spatial character are transformed between the positive and negative versions.

"Ascension" lives in the world of emergence, elevation, expansion, and light. Its sounds are designed to feel as though they are pulling upward and opening outward. Longer tonal elements, rising textures, resonances, and brighter high-frequency detail help reinforce the sense of movement and transformation.

"Exodus" takes that same conceptual DNA and turns it inside out. Sounds become darker, heavier, more restrained, and more gravitational. Where Ascension suggests expansion, Exodus suggests contraction. Where one rises, the other falls.

A major part of the process was building the sound effects around the physical movement of the visuals. Every transition, distortion, flicker, rotation, flash, and change in form became an opportunity for a sonic event. Impacts were synchronized to visual hits, granular textures followed digital artifacts, tonal sweeps reinforced movement through space, and subtle environmental layers helped give the abstract imagery a sense of physical presence.

I wanted the sound design to respond to the black-and-white inversion itself. The visual negative isn't simply a different grade—it changes how the image feels. I treated the audio in the same way.

The two tracks share DNA, but their emotional frequencies are reversed.

The goal was for the two pieces to feel like they could exist independently, while revealing something completely different when experienced together—as two reflections of the same sonic and visual object.

Sound Design/Music @abelokugawa

caption_text:
I was very happy to design the structure of the headpiece "Galaxea" before the artists @murielnisse & @yiqingyin work their magic on it.

The result of this collaboration is a sculptural cadavre exquis where each gesture naturally flows into the next, gradually assembling into a multilayered organic form.

A constellation of savoir‑faire and dialogues with the intelligence of the hand: 3D printing, artisanal pleating, needle embroidery, hair work, and structurally dyed satin.

One of the first creations of @odess_studio shot by myself.

caption_text:
This fluid study was built around a custom 2D Pyro workflow.

The idea originally came from an R&D task I was working on for a client project earlier this year. I liked the underlying behavior enough to revisit it later and push the technique further as a personal experiment.

I first created an initial simulation focused on the main velocity field, while also generating UVs internally as an additional 2D Pyro field. That first sim then became the advection driver for the bubbles and their velocity, allowing them to inherit the motion and flow of the fluid in a more natural way.

After that, I created a second fluid simulation using only the velocity from the first Pyro setup, combined with collisions and bubble velocity. This made the fluid react to spheres moving across its surface, changing the internal mixing and creating more dynamic interaction.

I also experimented with a non-divergent workflow in COPs, but for this particular look it was missing some of the organic, naturally unstable motion that I still get from the old 2D Pyro Solver.

A fun experiment in using Pyro not only as smoke, but as a flexible field-based solver for art-directable fluid motion and procedural detail.

caption_text:
This fluid study was built around a custom 2D Pyro workflow.

The idea originally came from an R&D task I was working on for a client project earlier this year. I liked the underlying behavior enough to revisit it later and push the technique further as a personal experiment.

I first created an initial simulation focused on the main velocity field, while also generating UVs internally as an additional 2D Pyro field. That first sim then became the advection driver for the bubbles and their velocity, allowing them to inherit the motion and flow of the fluid in a more natural way.

After that, I created a second fluid simulation using only the velocity from the first Pyro setup, combined with collisions and bubble velocity. This made the fluid react to spheres moving across its surface, changing the internal mixing and creating more dynamic interaction.

I also experimented with a non-divergent workflow in COPs, but for this particular look it was missing some of the organic, naturally unstable motion that I still get from the old 2D Pyro Solver.

A fun experiment in using Pyro not only as smoke, but as a flexible field-based solver for art-directable fluid motion and procedural detail.

caption_text:
This fluid study was built around a custom 2D Pyro workflow.

The idea originally came from an R&D task I was working on for a client project earlier this year. I liked the underlying behavior enough to revisit it later and push the technique further as a personal experiment.

I first created an initial simulation focused on the main velocity field, while also generating UVs internally as an additional 2D Pyro field. That first sim then became the advection driver for the bubbles and their velocity, allowing them to inherit the motion and flow of the fluid in a more natural way.

After that, I created a second fluid simulation using only the velocity from the first Pyro setup, combined with collisions and bubble velocity. This made the fluid react to spheres moving across its surface, changing the internal mixing and creating more dynamic interaction.

I also experimented with a non-divergent workflow in COPs, but for this particular look it was missing some of the organic, naturally unstable motion that I still get from the old 2D Pyro Solver.

A fun experiment in using Pyro not only as smoke, but as a flexible field-based solver for art-directable fluid motion and procedural detail.

caption_text:
I’m sharing a free @cavalry.app script that adds new features to the built-in Convex Hull tool.
You can add obstacle shapes and control the overall form to create different variations.
The source code is available, so you can download it, edit it, and customize it for your own needs.
My previous Soft Cell script is also now open source.
I’ve been extremely busy recently and probably won’t have much time to maintain or fix bugs, so I decided to share everything openly instead.
I hope these two scripts can help with your learning and creative process!
Link in bio.

caption_text:
Been messing around with some cell-style animation lately and somehow ended up making a whole @cavalry.app script 😅
It’s mainly built with JS Shapes, and tbh, Codex did most of the coding. I was basically the ideas guy—testing stuff, breaking stuff, and asking for endless changes until it finally worked lol.
Definitely not calling myself a “developer” here. I just wanted a nice little system that makes it easier for me to animate this kind of thing. The result is giving slightly cursed Voronoi shader vibes 👀
If anyone wants to try it, feel free to DM me and I’ll send you the free version. 
No promises on bug fixes though 😂
